note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  
  • Low appetite (~3.5 mo)  
  • Fatigue/low energy, headaches, occasional nausea  
  • Unintentional weight loss ≈1 stone (~6 kg) over ~6 mo  
  • Episodic palpitations and perceived breathlessness in elevators (no exertional dyspnoea or chest pain)  
  • Past history of primary hypothyroidism; levothyroxine discontinued several months ago  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  
  • Levothyroxine – stopped; dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • No other medications reported  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Decreased libido (“wife complaining about nightly activities”)  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  
  • Sedentary recently (“haven’t been walking lately”)  
  • Occupation: lawyer; job change 3.5 mo ago  
  • No information on diet, tobacco, alcohol, or other substances – not recorded  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  
  • Low mood (“feeling down”)  
  • Hesitant to label as “depressed”; no self-harm thoughts asked or disclosed  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  
  • Married; home life “OK”  
  • Work stress related to new law firm  
  • Secure housing; no financial stressors documented  

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded (weight change only provided)  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Not recorded  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Planned comprehensive panel (CBC, U&E, LFTs, vitamin levels, thyroid profile) – not yet performed  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Planned within above panel  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not applicable (male)  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not applicable  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not recorded  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not recorded  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 35-y-o man with untreated hypothyroidism, low mood, anorexia, weight loss, and situational palpitations.  
• No red-flag GI or cardiorespiratory symptoms; bowels normal; no chest pain.  

Working diagnosis  
1. Major depressive disorder with somatic symptoms – supported by low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight change, fatigue; temporally related to job change.  
2. Possible relapsed hypothyroidism after stopping levothyroxine – could account for fatigue and mood change; weight loss atypical but warrants thyroid function testing.  

Considerations  
• Iron-deficiency or other anaemia (fatigue, headaches)  
• Panic attacks / anxiety disorder (situational palpitations in lift)  

Plan  
• Arrange blood tests (CBC, iron studies, B12/folate, U&E, LFT, TSH, free T4, fasting glucose/lipids).  
• Review results; if hypothyroid, recommence levothyroxine per guidelines.  
• Perform full physical examination at follow-up.  
• Screen formally for depression/anxiety (e.g., PHQ-9, GAD-7) and assess suicide risk.  
• Safety-netting: attend ED for chest pain or worsening palpitations; re-contact clinic for GI changes or vomiting.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Advised on importance of blood tests and to seek urgent care for chest pain/palpitations; no further education documented.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Not recorded  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Pathology collection arranged via support line for blood tests  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  To book follow-up appointment when pathology results available; earlier if symptoms worsen  

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  mental_health_support_or_not_recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  specialist_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  dental_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  optometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  audiometry_referral_or_not_recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  social_support_referral_or_not_recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Major depressive disorder – High likelihood: persistent low mood, anhedonia, appetite/weight loss, fatigue temporal to work stress.  
2. Relapsed hypothyroidism – Medium likelihood: history of primary hypothyroidism, cessation of levothyroxine; compatible with fatigue/mood change.  
3. Iron-deficiency or other anaemia – Medium likelihood: fatigue, headaches; weight loss could reflect underlying anaemia; requires CBC/iron studies.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, BMI, complete lifestyle history (smoking, alcohol, diet, physical activity), immunisation review, chronic disease screening (diabetes, CVD risk, cancer screening).  
● Internal conflicts: weight loss atypical for hypothyroidism (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: clear audio; no physical exam performed; limited social and lifestyle history obtained.
